devotionals.title: Sustained by Grace
devotionals.scriptureText: He will also keep you firm to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. God is faithful, who has called you into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. 1 Corinthians 1:8-9
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Paul begins his letter by reminding the Corinthians of the grace that already defines them. He anchors them in what God has done for them through Christ. They are “sanctified in Christ Jesus,” “called to be his holy people,” and “enriched in every way.” Their identity is rooted in God’s initiative and not in their performance. Paul wants them to see that the God who called them is the God who equips and sustains them. This holds true for us today. Grace is not only the starting point; it is the steady foundation beneath our entire life.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. We are called by God’s grace. Paul begins with who they are in Christ. The Corinthians were inconsistent and divided, yet Paul calls them holy because God had set them apart. Our calling rests on God’s grace, not our perfection. He names us before He shapes us.

2. God has enriched us for every season. Paul reminds the Corinthian church that God has already supplied all the gifts, wisdom, and spiritual strength that they need. Their challenge was not lack of provision but lack of alignment. The same is true for us. God equips His people, even when we feel unprepared or inadequate.

3. God’s faithfulness keeps us firm to the end. This passage grounds our confidence in God’s unwavering faithfulness. The One who called us will sustain us. The One who began the work will complete it. Our hope rests in His commitment, not our consistency.

Today’s passage invites us to rest in the God who calls, enriches, and sustains. Before we face our weaknesses, we remember His strength. Before we confront our failures, we remember His faithfulness. In every season, we are sustained by Grace.

\
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for enriching my life with Your grace. Please keep me steady by Your faithfulness and strengthen me to walk in the calling You’ve given.

devotionals.title: United in Christ
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Paul addresses one of the church’s deepest wounds: division. The Corinthians were gathering around personalities, preferences, and gifted leaders, allowing their loyalties to fracture their fellowship. Paul does not dismiss their differences, but he calls them back to Christ. Our unity is not meant to rest on human leaders but on the One who was crucified for us. Paul’s appeal is gentle but firm: let Christ, not preference, shape your community.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Unity is a calling, not a convenience. Paul urges the believers toward a unity rooted in shared conviction and shared devotion to Christ. This unity is neither uniformity nor the absence of disagreement. It is the commitment to place Christ above personal preference. Unity is something we pursue because it reflects the heart of the One who saved us.

2. Division grows when we elevate people above Christ. The Corinthians were attaching themselves to gifted leaders, turning admiration into allegiance. Paul reminds them that no human leader was crucified for them. No pastor, teacher, or mentor can take the place of Christ. Jesus alone deserves our devotion.

3. The power of the gospel rests in Christ, not human skill. Paul refuses to build his ministry on personality or rhetorical brilliance. The gospel’s power does not depend on human wisdom but on divine truth. Christ is the message, and Christ is the power behind the message. When He is central, everything else finds its proper place.

Today’s passage invites us to examine our loyalties and our loves. Are we gathering around Christ or around personalities? Are we shaped by the gospel or by preference? Unity is possible when Christ is our center, and His cross is our anchor.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please keep my heart centered on Christ alone. Teach me to pursue unity with humility, and let the power of the gospel shape my life.

devotionals.title: The Wisdom of the Cross
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul draws a sharp and beautiful contrast between the wisdom of the world and the wisdom of God. To some, the message of the cross appears weak, foolish, or unnecessary. But to those who are being saved, it is the very power of God. Paul wants the Corinthians church to see that God’s wisdom does not follow human patterns. The cross stands at the center of the Christian life as the place where God’s power is revealed most clearly.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. The cross reveals God’s power in unexpected ways. The cross does not fit human categories. It looks like defeat and weakness. Yet it is victory.  It is strength. God’s power is not always loud or impressive by human standards. Sometimes it looks like surrender, sacrifice, and love poured out.

2. God overturns human wisdom. God is not impressed by human brilliance. The gospel does not rest on intellectual achievement or philosophical skill. God’s wisdom humbles the proud and lifts the humble. He chooses what seems small to accomplish what is great.

3. Christ is the wisdom and power of God. The cross of Christ is God’s chosen way of saving the world. In Christ, God’s wisdom takes on flesh. His power is revealed through sacrifice. What the world calls foolish, God calls salvation.

Today’s passage invites us to embrace the wisdom of the cross. We do not measure God’s work by human standards. We do not judge His power by outward strength. We look to Christ, and we find in Him the wisdom that leads to life.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please teach me to trust the wisdom of the cross. Let Christ be my wisdom, my power, and my confidence in every season.

devotionals.title: Chosen by Grace
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul invites the Corinthians to look honestly at their own story. Many of them were not influential, powerful, or impressive by the world’s standards. Yet God chose them and brought them into His family. Our place in God’s kingdom is not the result of human strength but divine grace. God delights in choosing what seems small so that His greatness is unmistakable. The cross has overturned human wisdom; it also overturns human boasting.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. God’s calling is not based on human status. Paul reminds the Corinthians that God did not choose them because they were impressive. Their story began with grace, not merit. God’s kingdom is not built on human credentials. He calls ordinary people so that His extraordinary power is seen clearly.

2. God uses what seems weak to display His strength. God’s choices often run opposite to human expectations. He delights in lifting the humble, strengthening the weak, and working through what the world overlooks. God’s power shines brightest through vessels that cannot claim the glory for themselves.

3. Christ is our wisdom, righteousness, holiness, and redemption. Our standing before God is a gift we did not earn. Christ is our wisdom, righteousness, holiness and redemption. Every spiritual blessing flows from Him. Therefore, the only rightful boast of the believer is the Lord Himself.

Today’s passage invites us to rest in the grace that chose us, shaped us, and continues to sustain us. We do not stand before God because of our strength, intelligence, or background. We stand because of Christ’s work, wisdom and righteousness. Hence, our boast is only in what He has done and nothing we can ever do.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for choosing me by Your grace. Please keep me humble, and teach me to rest in Christ alone.

devotionals.title: Strength in Simplicity
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul reminds the Corinthians how he first came to them, not with polished speech, impressive rhetoric, or human brilliance, but with a simple message: Jesus Christ and Him crucified. The power of the gospel does not rest on the skill of the messenger but on the Spirit who works through the message.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. God works through humble dependence. Paul does not hide his limitations. He embraces them. Our weakness is not a barrier to God’s work. It is rather the very place where God’s power could be seen clearly. God often does His deepest work through hearts that lean on Him rather than on themselves.

2. The message of Christ is the center of our witness. Paul made a deliberate choice to keep the gospel central. He refused to let style overshadow substance. The cross is not one topic among many; it was the heartbeat of Christian ministry. Our lives and words carry power when Christ remains at the center.

3. True spiritual power comes from the Spirit, not human skill. Paul wanted the Corinthians faith to rest on God, not on him. The Spirit is the One who opens hearts, convicts, strengthens, and saves. Human eloquence may impress, but only the Spirit transforms. When we rely on Him, our weakness becomes a platform for His strength.

Today’s passage invites us to embrace simplicity, humility, and dependence on God. We do not need to be impressive for God to use us. We simply need to keep Christ at the center and trust the Spirit to do what only He can do.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please teach me to always rely on Your Spirit rather than my own strength. Help me to keep Christ at the center of my life and witness.

devotionals.title: Wisdom Prepared for Us
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul directs our attention to the wisdom God has prepared for His people. The Corinthians admired intellect, eloquence, and philosophical depth, but Paul reminds them that God’s wisdom is of a different kind; it’s eternal, hidden, and revealed only by the Spirit. What God has prepared for His children is far greater than anything the world could imagine or achieve.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. God’s wisdom is reserved for the mature. True maturity is not measured by intellectual achievement but by spiritual openness. Those who are growing in Christ learn to value what God values and to see beyond the surface of things. God’s wisdom becomes clear as our hearts are shaped by Him.

2. God’s wisdom is eternal and hidden from the world. Human rulers and systems cannot grasp the wisdom of God. His purposes often run counter to human expectations. His wisdom is not discovered through analysis but revealed through grace. What He has prepared for His people is beyond human imagination.

3. The Spirit reveals what God has prepared for us. The Spirit searches the deep things of God and makes them known to us. Without Him, we remain blind to God’s purposes. With Him, we begin to see the beauty, depth, and richness of what God has planned. The Spirit opens our eyes to the wisdom of Christ.

Today’s passage invites us to be open and receive the wisdom God offers. We do not grasp it by striving; we receive it by the Spirit. God has prepared more for us than we can imagine, and He delights to reveal it to those who seek Him with humble hearts.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please open my heart to Your wisdom. Teach me to value what You value and to see beyond what the world celebrates.

devotionals.title: Revealed by the Spirit
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul shows the Corinthians that God’s wisdom cannot be grasped through human effort. The Corinthians were tempted to evaluate spiritual truth through human intellect, eloquence, and cultural sophistication but Paul reminds them that spiritual understanding is made possible by the Spirit of God. The Spirit opens our eyes, shapes our discernment, and teaches us to see with the mind of Christ. Without the Spirit, we remain limited by our own perspective, unable to truly comprehend the mysteries of God.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Only the Spirit reveals the depths of God. Human wisdom can observe, analyze, and speculate, but it cannot uncover the heart of God. Spiritual truth comes by revelation. The Spirit alone knows the depths of God and He alone can make those depths known to us.

2. We have received the Spirit so we can understand what God has given. Spiritual understanding is freely given by God. The Spirit helps us grasp grace, recognize God’s gifts, and see the world through a new lens. What once seemed foolish now becomes precious. What once seemed hidden now becomes clear.

3. The mind of Christ shapes how we discern and live. The Spirit forms within us the mind of Christ; His humility, His discernment, His priorities and His way of seeing. Spiritual maturity is about becoming more like Christ. With the mind of Christ, we learn to judge rightly, love deeply, and walk wisely.

Today’s passage invites us to listen to the Spirit as we journey on in life. We do not navigate life by human insight alone. We walk with the One who knows the heart of God and shapes us to think, discern, and live with the mind of Christ.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please open my heart to the things of Your Spirit. Teach me to see with the mind of Christ and shape my thoughts, desires, and decisions according to Your wisdom.

devotionals.title: Growing Into Maturity
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul tells the Corinthians that he could not address them as mature believers because their lives were still shaped by jealousy, rivalry, and comparison. Their divisions were signs of spiritual immaturity. Paul is inviting them to grow. He wants them to see that the gospel does not only saves us but also shapes us, moving us from childish patterns into Christ-like maturity.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Spiritual maturity is measured by character, not just knowledge. The Corinthians had spiritual gifts, insight, and teaching, yet Paul calls them infants in Christ. Why? Because maturity is not about what we know but how we live out what we know. Jealousy, pride, and rivalry reveal a heart still shaped by the world. Growth in Christ shows up in humility, patience, and love.

2. Immaturity shows itself in how we relate to others. The Corinthians’ conflicts were symptoms of a heart not yet surrendered to the Spirit’s shaping. When comparison drives us, when rivalry defines us, when jealousy fuels us, we are living from the flesh, not the Spirit. Our relationships reveal our spiritual condition more clearly than our words.

3. Christ frees us from comparison and calls us into unity. In Christ, we are freed from the need to prove ourselves or attach ourselves to personalities. Maturity grows when Christ becomes our center, and His Spirit shapes our identity. Unity becomes possible when comparison gives way.

Today’s passage invites us to examine the places where immaturity still lingers in our hearts. The Spirit is patient. He grows us. He forms Christ in us. And He leads us from rivalry into unity, from jealousy into joy and from childishness into maturity.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please grow me into maturity. Shape my character by Your Spirit, and teach me to walk in humility, unity, and love.
